### StarCraft II (`sc2`)

Written in the batch R4 preparation, before any `sc2` unit is coded, for multiplayer at patch 5.0.17. Sources: the StarCraft Wiki read through its API (unit pages, Template:UnitBox, Template:UnitAgmtBox/doc), Blizzard's patch notes on news.blizzard.com, the official site starcraft2.blizzard.com, and the Liquipedia pages already in the page cache (nothing was requested from liquipedia.net).

- **Official text: the in-game description and the help panel.** The game gives each unit a short description line, and its in-game help lists three units it is strong against and three it is weak against. No separate designation line was found. No manual with unit text was found, and the official site has no unit pages: starcraft2.blizzard.com shows race overviews only, and its address for units gives a not-found page (checked 11 November 2026). Blizzard's patch notes are official text too; they seldom name a unit's job, but a design note that does counts for step 1.
- **Where to read it: Liquipedia only, and only from the cache.** Liquipedia's `Infobox unit` holds the description in its `description` field, which reads as the game's own line (the template's documentation was not read, since Liquipedia is not requested), and the help lists in its `strong` and `weak` fields; on the Raven and Reaper pages an editor's comment beside the lists says they follow the in-game help. Cite such a page as kind wiki, with a note that the field copies in-game text. The cached SC2 unit pages are: https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Baneling (also Baneling_(Legacy_of_the_Void)), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Carrier, https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Corrosive_Bile (a redirect: the file holds the Ravager page), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Raven_(Legacy_of_the_Void), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Reaper_(Legacy_of_the_Void), https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Swarm_Host, https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Prismatic_Alignment (a redirect: the file holds the Void Ray page) and https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Warp_Prism_(Legacy_of_the_Void). Cite each under the address its cache file records.
- **Every other unit has no readable official line in this batch.** Step 1 gives nothing, so go on to step 2. Add an uncertain entry at roles/primary saying the in-game description could not be read (Liquipedia not requested), so the merge pass can revisit it if Mustafa allows a way to read Liquipedia.
- **The StarCraft Wiki does not carry the description.** Template:UnitBox has no field for it. Its `role` field is the wiki's own words, mixing lore, the pre-release site and paraphrase: the Marine's general-purpose light infantry, the Siege Tank's three lines, from heavy infantry tank to mobile artillery, the Raven's aerial support unit, the Carrier's capital ship; the Adept's is empty. The ability boxes (Template:UnitAgmtBox) have a `desc` field that the template's documentation calls only a description of the ability, not game text: treat it as the wiki's words, as the R1 note does for the Command & Conquer Wiki's ability boxes. The Game Unit prose that names what a unit is strong or weak against (Zealot, Carrier, Raven pages) is the wiki's own and does not follow the help panel: the Raven's prose names the Siege Tank, while the cached help-panel list names the Dark Templar, Banshee and Roach. The quote box at the top of a unit page is a voice line or lore, often from a campaign (Abathur on the Lurker page): never role text, and never copied.
- **Roles step 1 reads the description line.** Only a role label or alias counts (vocabularies, Roles). The cached lines: the Reaper's opens with Raider (raider, if its stock speed meets raider's requires); the Swarm Host's calls it a siege unit and the Ravager's ranged artillery (siege, which must still pass its coding rule); the Warp Prism's calls it a flying transport (transport, a role with no target); the Raven's aerial support names support, which the Raven can claim only if it meets support's requires (a repair tool, or a heal, repair or resupply pattern), so otherwise step 1 skips it; the Carrier's capital ship, the Void Ray's surgical strike craft and the Baneling's kamikaze unit name none.
- **Strong and weak lists (roles step 4, the secondary drop rule, matchups).** The help panel's lists name units, never kinds of target, so they give no strong-against text for step 4 and drop no role under roles.secondary, as the R1 note rules for named units in Red Alert's manual. They are official text that names a matchup: use them in counters and countered by, naming the other unit by what decides the matchup (Matchups rule 1). The Reaper's strong list is the three workers; its weak list the Stalker, Marauder and Roach.
- **So step 4 rests on the game data.** Each weapon's extra damage is tied to an attribute and added per hit before armour (StarCraft Wiki, Attributes). Read a bonus against Armored as a bonus against armour (anti-armour; buildings are Armored too) and a bonus against Light as a bonus against anti-infantry's target, which the word list gives as soldiers and light targets. A bonus against Biological, Mechanical, Psionic, Massive or Structure, or the Widow Mine's extra damage to shields, names none of the three targets. A weapon whose infobox row is marked for Air only can hit nothing else, so it gives anti-air.

### StarCraft II (`sc2`)

Rewritten in the batch R4 preparation for multiplayer at patch 5.0.17 (it replaces the pilot list), before any `sc2` unit is coded. Sources, read on 11 November 2026: the StarCraft Wiki (https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/<Title>, through its API) pages Attributes, Armored, Massive, Cloaking, Detector, Burrow, Creep, Larva (StarCraft II), Plasma shield, Supply, Hotkey, Tech lab, Reactor, Gateway (its Warp Gate section), Overlord (StarCraft II), Overseer, Medivac dropship, Warp prism, Bunker, Nydus network, Nydus worm, SCV (StarCraft II), Zergling (StarCraft II), Infestor, Viper, Engineering bay, Armory, Evolution chamber, Forge, Cybernetics core, Spire, Orbital command, Nexus, Xel'naga tower, Colossus, Mothership and StarCraft II Q&A batches/40, with Template:UnitBox for its field labels; Blizzard's patch notes 5.0.15 to 5.0.17 with their hotfixes; and the cached Liquipedia Burrow and Reaper (Legacy of the Void) pages.

- **Basic orders** (no pattern): every unit has move, stop, hold position, patrol, attack and attack-move, and hold fire and weapons free (the Hotkey page's universal abilities). Load and unload are universal keys. The list has no stance, retreat or reinforce order. Gather, return cargo and build belong to the workers, which are not coded. Turning an ability's autocast on or off is part of that ability, not an entry of its own.
- **No veterancy:** no page read gives a versus unit ranks or experience; the infobox's Meta group holds only target priority and scores. No `earn-veterancy`, and no ability has source veterancy.
- **Supply** (no pattern): every unit uses supply from a pool capped at 200, raised by Supply Depots, Overlords, Pylons and town halls (Supply page, which notes that Zerg control and Protoss psi work the same way; the Overlord's infobox gives the supply it adds). Leave it off: cost_band.raw already leaves population out. The Overlord's supply belongs to this shared mechanic: say it in its notes, not as an ability.
- **Attributes and bonus damage** (how coders read the game data): a unit is ground or air; light, armored or neither; biological, mechanical, both (the Hellbat) or neither (the Archon); and some also carry Massive, Psionic, Detector, Structure or Summoned (Attributes page). Bonus damage is set per attribute and added to each hit before armour; buildings count as Armored. The game has no damage_map, so armament damage takes step 5, where a bonus against Armored is a bonus against armoured targets; roles step 4 is under Official role lines. A unit's attributes set its armour class at step 2 (Damage and armour maps, above). The Attributes page lags on the Ghost, which has carried Light since 5.0.15 (patch notes; its own page marks Light for versus only).
  - **Flat armour** (armour model `damage-reduction`): the game takes each unit's armour value off every hit. A Marine's rifle hit is 6 (Marine page), so stock armour of 2 or more takes off a quarter or more: code damage-reduction on such units of class medium or heavier, and mention 1 point of armour in armour.notes only.
  - **Massive:** the biggest units (in versus the Archon, Carrier, Colossus, Mothership, Tempest, Battlecruiser, Thor, Brood Lord and Ultralisk) break Force Fields by walking into them, fill 8 transport slots, and are not affected by Force Field, Concussive Shells or Graviton Beam (Massive page). Say so in their strengths, linking `immune:` to the pattern that the Sentry's or Phoenix's entry links for that ability, or naming the effect in the reason where no pattern fits.
- **Energy** (resource `energy`): casters carry an energy bar that refills slowly and pays for their abilities, and a Terran cloak drains it while on (Cloaking page). Code energy on every unit whose StarCraft Wiki infobox gives a Maximum energy line for versus (among them the Ghost, Medivac, Raven, Phoenix, Sentry, High Templar, Infestor, Viper and Overseer), and on no unit whose abilities run on cooldowns only. An energy cost is not a cooldown: give a cooldown band only from a cooldown figure. The Ghost's EMP drains energy and shields in an area and the High Templar's Feedback punishes energy users (the EMP Shot box on the Detector page; the High templar page); the Nexus's Energy Recharge refills a unit's energy (a side-wide power, below).
- **Cloaking and detection:** a cloaked or burrowed enemy cannot be targeted unless a detector is near, though a faint ripple can give it away and splash damage still hits it; a cloaked unit keeps its cloak while it attacks (Cloaking page). Record each cloak on its unit with `cloak`, and say in the summary that firing does not break it, since the pattern's summary has the cloak end on attack.
  - Always cloaked: the Dark Templar and the Observer (5.0.15 says Surveillance mode now reveals the Observer: check its page and say so in that mode's summary). A passive ability, source innate; no stealth trait, because cloak is the fully invisible case (sensor traits).
  - Cloak researched and switched on: the Ghost (Personal Cloaking, at the Ghost Academy) and the Banshee (Cloaking Field). Source upgrade, linking `cloak` and `upgrade-in-field`; both use energy while cloaked.
  - The Mothership cloaks friendly units and buildings near it, but not itself: record that on the Mothership.
  - Detectors (sensor trait `detector`): the Raven, Overseer and Observer among units; the infobox's Detection range line marks them (Detector page; Template:UnitBox). Missile Turrets, Spore Crawlers, Photon Cannons and the Orbital Command's Scanner Sweep detect too. The Oracle's Revelation reveals for a time: an ability linking `reveal-area`. Abilities whose effect also reveals say so in their summaries: EMP shows cloaked units for a moment but not burrowed ones, and Fungal Growth shows both (the boxes on the Detector page). In a cloaked unit's countered_by, link `sensor:detector` and name the buildings and Scanner Sweep in the reason.
- **Burrow** (pattern `burrow`, mobility trait `burrow`): the Burrow research at the Hatchery lets nearly every Zerg ground unit burrow; only the Larva, Egg, Cocoon, Broodling, Nydus Worm, Changeling and Locust cannot (cached Liquipedia Burrow page; the box on the StarCraft Wiki's Burrow page that leaves out the Ultralisk carries older text: it also names the Defiler, a unit of the first game). A burrowed unit can be targeted only with detection or under Fungal Growth, cannot move or attack unless its own entry says so, and sees less, except the Baneling and Swarm Host. Leave burrow off units that only have the shared version. Record it on units that do more: the Roach (moves and heals faster while burrowed once Tunneling Claws, a separate research at the Roach Warren, is done), the Infestor (moves and casts while burrowed), the Lurker (attacks only while burrowed), the Baneling (can lie burrowed as a mine and blow up from there) and the Swarm Host (spawns Locusts while burrowed, cached Liquipedia Swarm Host page). The Terran Widow Mine burrows with a button of its own: its own ability.
- **High ground** (no pattern): the game gives no combat bonus for terrain; a ground unit cannot see up a cliff without sight from a flier or a unit standing up there, so units firing from above cannot be fired back at until they are spotted (StarCraft II Q&A batches/40, a Blizzard answer the wiki copies; the Colossus page says the same of Stalkers on a cliff). Fliers see over cliffs. Leave it off. Units that cross or see past cliffs record it themselves: the Reaper's cliff jumps, the Colossus's cliff walking (the climb trait; a jump is not climb), the Stalker's Blink (`teleport`). The Colossus also sees the top of a cliff and, unlike other ranged units, can be shot from below while it stands on one (Colossus page).
- **Air and ground targeting:** every unit is ground or air (Attributes page), and each weapon row of the StarCraft Wiki infobox is marked for Ground, Air or both. The game has one air layer, which only weapons marked for Air reach.
  - can_target: a Ground mark is the weapon's own target line, since the row names the weapon, so it lists infantry and ground vehicles, and structures too when the weapon's family allows them (can_target step 3); an Air mark lists low air and high air. The game has no ships: never naval.
  - Mobility: every flier can stop and hold still (stop and hold position are universal orders), so code hovering flight, not jet, and add a fit_note at mobility/base saying that the game's fliers hover yet only weapons marked for Air reach them. Slow fliers (the Overlord, Overseer, Observer, Brood Lord, Carrier and Mothership among them) break that term's speed rule: record the break in atypical.
  - Matchups: name fliers as `class:aircraft` (one layer; Matchups rule 2).
  - The Colossus is a ground unit that weapons marked for Air can also hit; the Colossus page says Blizzard confirmed it. Say so in its weaknesses and put anti-air units in its countered_by. A unit whose mode changes its layer (the Viking lands in assault mode) gives the layer per mode.
- **Add-ons** (no pattern): a Barracks, Factory or Starport takes a Tech Lab (advanced units and research) or a Reactor (two units at once), never both (Tech lab and Reactor pages). Not a tier step (tier map). Name a needed Tech Lab in tier.basis; record nothing on the unit.
- **Warp-in** (`drop-in-from-above` would fit; left off): once Warp Gate is researched, the Zealot, Sentry, Stalker, Adept, Dark Templar and High Templar can be warped onto any power field of a Pylon or of a Warp Prism in phasing mode (Gateway page, Warp Gate section); since 5.0.17 a warp takes 3.6 seconds in fast fields and 11 in slow ones (patch notes); the Gateway page adds that a warp-in fed by a Warp Prism is cancelled, with a refund, if the Prism dies. Leave warp-in off those units. The phasing mode that makes the field is the Warp Prism's own mode.
- **Larva and eggs** (no pattern): most Zerg units hatch from Larva at a Hatchery, Lair or Hive; the Queen is not made from Larva, and the Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Overseer and Brood Lord are morphed from other units (Larva (StarCraft II) page). Production stays off every unit; the Larva and the Cocoon are not units (plan).
- **Morphing and merging: not game-wide.** Five units turn, at a price, into another unit that the plan codes on its own: Zergling to Baneling, Roach to Ravager, Hydralisk to Lurker, Corruptor to Brood Lord, Overlord to Overseer; and two templar merge into an Archon. The button belongs to the parent: record it there as an active ability, source innate (name the tech it needs in the summary), with no pattern and a fit_note naming the pattern wanted (turn into a different, stronger unit in the field). The child names its parent in tier.basis and cost_band.basis, and its price includes the parent's (cost_thresholds basis). The Overlord's transport morph only adds seats to the same unit (Transports, below). The Hellion and the Hellbat change back and forth: that is for the unit list to settle.
- **Creep** (no pattern): Zerg ground units move faster on creep, most by about a third (the infobox's Creep multiplier: 1.3 for the Zergling); Queens and some others gain far more, Drones and fliers nothing, and creep belongs to no player, so an enemy Zerg uses it too (Creep page). Speeds are taken off creep (Speed, above); say in mobility.notes when a unit's multiplier differs from the usual. Spreading creep belongs to the units that do it (the Overlord's Generate Creep, and the unit that places creep tumours). Hatcheries and Nydus Worms make creep too, and other races cannot build on it.
- **Transports** (universal keys; `carry-passengers` on the carrier): the Medivac and the Warp Prism have 8 cargo slots, and an Overlord gets 8 once it buys its own transport morph (Mutate Ventral Sacs, which needs a Lair; since Legacy of the Void each Overlord buys it for itself: Overlord (StarCraft II) page). A rider fills slots by its size, from 1 (the Marine, the Zergling) to 8 (Massive units); each infobox gives the unit's size. Code crew.passengers.seats as the carrier's slot count, kind passenger-cargo, since no page shows riders firing out; give the slot sizes in crew.notes. The Overlord's seats come only from that purchase, so its seat passive is source upgrade and links `carry-passengers` and `upgrade-in-field`. Loading and unloading are universal keys; the Load Nearby command that 5.0.16 gave the Medivac, Warp Prism and Overlord was taken out again by the 5.0.16b hotfix, so it is not in the version researched. Buildings that hold units are not coded: in a Bunker soldiers fire with one more point of range (that bonus stays off; range bands use the unit in the open), the Nydus system keeps units out of reach until every entrance is gone, and a Command Center holds five SCVs. No page read says what happens to riders when a Medivac, Warp Prism or Overlord is destroyed: write nothing about it unless the unit's own page does.
- **Salvage and lift-off** (buildings only): salvaging a Bunker and lifting off a Terran production building or town hall are building actions; no unit has them. Leave them off.
- **Plasma shields** (armour model `regen-shield`): every Protoss unit has shields over its health; they refill quickly after a short spell without damage, suffer whatever bonus damage the unit beneath would take, and EMP drains them (Plasma shield page). Code regen-shield on each Protoss unit, as the term's examples say, and put Forge shield levels in armour.notes. Shield Batteries are buildings.
- **Zerg regeneration** (armour model `self-repair`): Zerg units slowly regain health; the infobox's hit point regen line gives the same small rate on the Zerg pages that fill it (Zergling, Infestor, Viper, Larva). Code self-repair on each Zerg unit and say in armour.notes that it is slow and shared by the race. The Roach heals much faster while burrowed (its own entry). Terran and Protoss health does not come back on its own, except the Reaper's, which heals out of combat by its in-game description (cached Liquipedia Reaper page): code self-repair on the Reaper.
- **Repair and healing by others** (nothing on the unit that receives it): SCVs and MULEs repair any friendly mechanical unit, Protoss ones included, and Terran buildings (SCV page; the 5.0.16 notes on MULE repair); Medivacs heal friendly biological units (Medivac dropship page). Record healing only on the unit that does it (the Medivac: `repair-allies`); workers and buildings are not coded, and being repairable is no armour model.
- **Class-wide upgrades** (side-wide, left off): weapon and armour levels bought for a whole class of units at the Engineering Bay (Terran infantry), Armory (vehicles and ships), Evolution Chamber (Zerg ground), Spire (Zerg fliers), Forge (Protoss ground units and every shield) and Cybernetics Core (Protoss air) (their pages). Bands use the stock unit; name levels in notes only where they turn a matchup.
- **Research for one unit type:** research done once at a building (Stimpack, Concussive Shells, Personal Cloaking, Blink, Charge, Burrow and the like) is source upgrade, even though it reaches every unit of the type (ability sources tie-break). It reaches units already fielded (the 5.0.15 notes fix a bug where Hi-Sec Auto Tracking failed to update its level on the icons of the units it affected), so a button or weapon it adds links `upgrade-in-field` (Paired entries). Research that only changes numbers (speed, range, health) goes in that field's notes.
- **Side-wide powers** (left off every unit): the Orbital Command's Scanner Sweep (reveals an area, hidden units included), MULE and Extra Supplies; the Nexus's Chrono Boost, Strategic Recall (pulls units back to a Nexus) and Energy Recharge (refills a unit's energy) (Orbital command and Nexus pages). None gives named unit types a new button, so no ability has source commander-power. Name them in matchups where they matter: Scanner Sweep against cloaked units, Energy Recharge for casters, Recall for a Protoss army that must escape.
- **Map features** (no pattern): a ground unit next to a Xel'Naga tower gives its side the tower's wide view; burrowed units and fliers cannot hold a tower, cloaked units can (Xel'naga tower page). Leave it off.
- **Caps** (availability): only the Mothership has a cap of its own, one per player at a time (Mothership page): availability limited, not unique, since it is no hero. Every other unit is open; the supply cap is shared.

registry_findings.current: Marine (Terran basic infantry): movement speed 3.15 as the wikis give it for versus mode (Faster game-speed values); keep every speed at the same game speed. Speeds and cooldowns are in Faster seconds, as Liquipedia gives them; divide Normal values by 1.4.
registry_findings.proposed: Marine (Terran basic infantry): movement speed 3.15 as the wikis give it for versus mode (Faster game-speed values); keep every speed at the same game speed. Speeds are distances per Faster second and cooldowns are Faster seconds, as Liquipedia and the StarCraft Wiki's versus lines give them. To convert a figure given at Normal game speed, multiply a speed by 1.4 and divide a duration by 1.4. Never use the StarCraft Wiki's Co-op lines, which are on the Normal scale (the Marine's 2.25).
registry_findings.evidence: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Marine_(StarCraft_II) (UnitBox, read through the API on 11 November 2026): the versus speed 3.15 stands beside a Co-op line of 2.25, and the versus rifle cooldown 0.61 beside a Co-op 0.86, which is the same unit at two scales: the versus speed is 1.4 times the other, the versus cooldown 1.4 times shorter. The UnitBox of https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Siege_tank_(StarCraft_II) (3.15 and 2.25; cooldown 0.74 and 1.04), https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Zergling_(StarCraft_II) (4.13 and 2.95) and https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overseer (2.62 and 1.88) show the same ratio. Blizzard's notes give speeds on the versus scale: https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24225313/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-patch-notes (Protoss list: Mothership 2.83 to 2.25), https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24240447/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-hotfix-patch-notes (Balance: Brood Lord 2.62 to 2.24) and https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (Ghost: 3.85 to 3.94). Dividing a Normal speed by 1.4, as the entry now says, would make the Marine's 2.25 about 1.6, half its versus figure, and would turn a medium unit very slow. The figure 3.15 itself is right: it is the Marine's 2.25 per game second at Faster speed, and its UnitBox gives an acceleration of 1000, so it moves at the listed speed from the start.

registry_findings.current: Price = minerals + 3 x gas: a saturated base mines about 925 minerals and 325 gas a minute (about 2.85 to 1), rounded to 3. Anchor: the Siege Tank, the game's only tank, 150 minerals and 125 gas, so 525; thresholds at 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the anchor, rounded to the nearest 10. Morphed units (Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Brood Lord, Archon) count the parent's price too.
registry_findings.proposed: Price = minerals + 3 x gas: a saturated base mines about 925 minerals and 325 gas a minute (about 2.85 to 1), rounded to 3. Anchor: the Siege Tank, the game's only tank, 150 minerals and 125 gas, so 525; thresholds at 0.5, 0.9, 1.4 and 2 times the anchor, rounded to the nearest 10. Morphed and merged units (Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Overseer, Brood Lord, Archon) count their parents' price too; the Archon comes to 1,000 whichever two templar merge.
registry_findings.evidence: docs/proposal.md, section 2.2 (Mustafa's answer of 11 November 2026) lists the Overseer with the Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Brood Lord and Archon as units that morph or merge from another unit and are units of their own, but the basis leaves it out. https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overseer (UnitBox): it evolves from the Overlord for 50 minerals and 50 gas and needs a Lair; https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overlord_(StarCraft_II) (UnitBox): the Overlord costs 100 minerals. With the parent the Overseer comes to 300, the low band; without it 200, very low, so the omission changes its band. https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/High_templar_(StarCraft_II) (50 and 150) and https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Dark_templar_(StarCraft_II) (125 and 125) each give 500 by the formula, so every pair that merges into an Archon gives 1,000.

notes.other_notes:
- **Version and patches.** Research patch 5.0.17 (7 October 2026). Read Blizzard's own notes, newest first, and take the latest figure for each value: 5.0.17 https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes; 5.0.16b hotfix (16 July 2026) https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24291949/starcraft-ii-5-0-16b-hotfix-patch-notes; 5.0.16 hotfix (30 June 2026) https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24289266/starcraft-ii-5-0-16-hotfix-patch-notes; 5.0.16 (22 June 2026) https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24259080/starcraft-ii-5-0-16-patch-notes; 5.0.15 hotfix (8 October 2025) https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24240447/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-hotfix-patch-notes; 5.0.15 (30 September 2025) https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24225313/starcraft-ii-5-0-15-patch-notes. The index https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/feed/starcraft-2 is plain HTML (the older address /en-us/starcraft2 redirects there). 5.0.17's developer note says most of 5.0.16's balance changes went back to 5.0.15, and its list undoes them item by item; changes its list does not mention, and so presumably still in force, include the Overseer's Changelings taking over its order queue and dying together, Neural Parasite on an SCV that is building lasting until the building is done, and rich geysers giving 6 a trip. The 5.0.16b hotfix had already removed Load Nearby and set the Ghost back to 2 supply.
- **Statements in this note that no longer hold** (its step-1 parts, checked on 11 November 2026):
  - "Liquipedia is the best source", with its one-parse-every-30-seconds advice, and the bullet about the blocked session: R4 requests nothing from liquipedia.net; only the cached pages may be read (Official role lines lists the unit pages).
  - "the in-game unit description in the Liquipedia and StarCraft Wiki infoboxes is official text": true only of Liquipedia's `description` field. The StarCraft Wiki's UnitBox has no such field, and its `role` field is the wiki's own words.
  - The patch list ("5.0.15, 5.0.16 and its hotfix, and 5.0.17") misses the 5.0.15 hotfix, which set the Brood Lord's speed, Psionic Storm and the Ghost's health, and the 5.0.16b hotfix. The rollback sentence holds, with the exceptions above.
  - Speed: "the wikis use Faster" holds for versus lines only; the StarCraft Wiki's co-op lines are on the Normal scale (registry finding on speed_reference). "Record those as abilities or upgrades": creep is game-wide and recorded nowhere, research that only adds speed goes in mobility.notes, and only a button such as Stimpack is an ability.
  - Pilot game-wide list: "Terran and Protoss units have none" (regeneration) misses the Reaper; the Roach moves underground only after Tunneling Claws; the regeneration and shield bullets were to be checked on Liquipedia and were checked on the StarCraft Wiki instead (Plasma shield page, hit point regen lines).
  - Armour rule (Damage and armour maps): it still holds, but the Ghost has carried Light since 5.0.15, so by the rule it is unarmoured, while the StarCraft Wiki's Attributes page still lists it as neither light nor armored; the Sentry is neither in versus (its page gives Light only for campaign and co-op): step 4. A Light, Biological creature bigger than small (the Mutalisk is the likely case) comes out unarmoured, which that class allows only for tiny and small bodies: record the break in atypical rather than pick another class.
- **Campaign and co-op statements that can go:** the tier bullet on campaign-only units (the WoL Firebat, Goliath, Diamondback and Wraith, the LotV Reaver) and its sentence on mission unlocks; nothing else in the note rests on them. verdicts.claim: Registry finding speed_reference: versus lines are on the Faster scale, Co-op lines on the Normal scale; convert Normal speeds by multiplying by 1.4
verdicts.reason: Every figure in the evidence checks out, and the current sentence would shrink speeds. One refinement: the StarCraft Wiki's per-second regen lines are on the Normal scale, so the proposed text should speak of speed and weapon-cooldown lines, not of versus lines in general (see missing).
verdicts.evidence: UnitBoxes read through the API: Marine 3.15 and 2.25 (Co-op), cooldown 0.61 and 0.86, accel 1000; Siege tank 3.15 and 2.25, cooldown 0.74 and 1.04; Zergling 4.13 and 2.95; Overseer 2.62 and 1.88. Blizzard notes: 5.0.15 Mothership 2.83 to 2.25; 5.0.15 hotfix Brood Lord 2.62 to 2.24; 5.0.17 Ghost 3.85 to 3.94. https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Cooldown (StarCraft II section): LotV aligned the values with the default game speed. The Observer's Co-op speed 1.88 against versus 2.82 (ratio 1.5) shows Co-op lines can differ in value as well as scale, another reason never to use them.
verdicts.correction: Marine (Terran basic infantry): movement speed 3.15 as the wikis give it for versus mode (Faster game-speed values); keep every speed at the same game speed. Speeds are distances per Faster second and weapon cooldowns are Faster seconds, as Liquipedia and the StarCraft Wiki's versus speed and cooldown lines give them. To convert a figure given at Normal game speed, multiply a speed by 1.4 and divide a duration by 1.4. Never use the StarCraft Wiki's Co-op lines (the Marine's 2.25), and treat its per-second regeneration lines as Normal-scale figures.

missing: Archon transport size: the Massive bullet and the Transports bullet both give Massive units 8 slots, but the Archon takes 4 (https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Archon_(StarCraft_II), UnitBox transsize 4; the Thor, Colossus and Ultralisk take 8).

Mothership in versus: its UnitBox type list includes Heroic, and the Infestor page's Neural Parasite box says Heroic units such as the Mothership cannot be taken over (https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Mothership UnitBox; https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Infestor rendered Neural Parasite box), so the attributes bullet should add Heroic for the Mothership. The same page gives its energy as None for versus and says 5.0.12 moved its abilities onto cooldowns, and its Cloaking Field box is a 20-second cast with a cooldown: the Mothership takes no energy resource and its cloak is an active ability.

Mutalisk regeneration: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Mutalisk_(StarCraft_II) UnitBox gives hit point regen 1.4 for versus, about five times the 0.2734 of other Zerg units, so the Zerg regeneration bullet needs a Mutalisk exception.

Roach and Tunneling Claws: Blizzard's 4.7.1 notes (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/22771167/starcraft-ii-4-7-1-patch-notes, Roach entry) removed Tunneling Claws' healing boost, and 5.0.16 ties the Rapid Regeneration icon to the Burrow research; the StarCraft Wiki Roach UnitBox still lists 10 with Tunneling Claws, a lagging value missing from the note's list of wiki lags.

Scale of the StarCraft Wiki's regeneration lines: its Roach UnitBox gives 5 burrowed and 10 with Tunneling Claws, exactly Blizzard's 7 and 14 HP a second divided by 1.4, so the wiki's per-second regen lines (hit points 0.2734, energy 0.5625, the Roach's 5) are Normal-scale while its speeds and weapon cooldowns are Faster (https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Roach; https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Cooldown StarCraft II section). The speed_reference text and the game-wide note should warn coders before they read a regen figure from the wiki.

Overlord speed lags: the 5.0.17 notes raise the Overlord's base speed from 0.85 to 0.9 (https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes, Zerg, Overlord), while https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overlord_(StarCraft_II) still gives 0.85 for versus; add it to the wiki values that lag (the band stays very slow either way).

Baneling parent price: a Baneling morphs from one Zergling, so its parent's price is 25 minerals, not the 50 of the two-Zergling purchase the Zergling bullet sets as cost_band.raw. Liquipedia's cached Baneling infobox gives a total of 50 minerals and 25 gas (https://liquipedia.net/starcraft2/Baneling), so 125 by the formula, not 150; same very-low band, but the basis should say which parent price counts.

candidates.name: Marine
candidates.teaches: The baseline rifleman: cheap and able to shoot ground and air alike. Its Stimpack spends some of its own health for a burst of speed and fire rate, so it leans on a healer (the Medivac). The clearest case of paying health for a timed boost.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Marine_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Stimpack and Combat Shield boxes; infobox)
https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (no Marine change at 5.0.17; the patch of record)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Barracks, no add-on. Stimpack and Combat Shield are researched at a Barracks tech lab. The infobox mixes co-op and campaign figures with the Versus ones: use Versus.
candidates.shooter_note: Cheap starter rifle that can hit fliers; one key trades health for a few seconds of sprint and rapid fire, so it lives or dies by its medic.
candidates.repeats: overclock-self is also on the Kirov (ra3) and the Voltaic Tank (tempest-rising); the Stimpack is the registry's own example for it (patterns.md).
candidates.role_guess: assault (generalist), anti-air as a secondary since it hits air

candidates.name: Marauder
candidates.teaches: Heavy infantry with bonus damage against armoured targets and no way to shoot fliers; a researched shell slows whatever it hits, so it can keep pace with and wear down retreating units. Teaches slow-on-hit kiting and a hard air blind spot.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Marauder (Versus: Concussive Shells and Stimpack boxes; infobox)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Barracks with a tech lab (the add-on is not a tier step). Concussive Shells and Stimpack are tech-lab research.
candidates.shooter_note: A sturdy anti-vehicle grenadier whose hits slow the target, so a patient player sticks to anyone fleeing; useless against anything in the air.
candidates.repeats: Shares the Marine's Stimpack (overclock-self); the slowing hit (weapon trait slow) and the total lack of anti-air are its own.

candidates.name: Reaper
candidates.teaches: A fast raider whose jet pack hops up and down cliffs, with a thrown charge that knocks enemies back after a short fuse and health that refills once it stops taking hits. Teaches terrain-ignoring harassment that disengages to heal.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Reaper (Versus: Combat Drugs, KD8 Charge and Jet Pack boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Barracks with no add-on (only the Wings of Liberty campaign asked for a tech lab). The out-of-combat healing is innate in versus.
candidates.shooter_note: Hit-and-run scout: jump a cliff into the backline, lob a knockback grenade to split foes, then drop back over a ledge to regenerate.
candidates.repeats: leap like the Sickle (ra3) and throw-explosive like Tanya (ra3) and Olga Morozova (iron-harvest); passive out-of-combat healing is the self-repair armour model, new in this pairing.

candidates.name: Ghost
candidates.teaches: A cloaking specialist with distinct tools: a slow-aimed sniper round that only hits living targets and, at 5.0.17, is broken off when the Ghost takes damage; an EMP that empties energy and strips shields in an area, friendly units included; and calling in a nuclear strike whose target is marked for a few seconds first. Teaches energy denial and a telegraphed strike carried by one soldier.

new_mechanics.summary: Hit an area or one enemy so its ability energy is emptied (in some versions its energy shields too), leaving casters unable to cast until it builds back; some versions turn the emptied energy into damage.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Ghost_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Steady Targeting, EMP Shot, Cloak and Nuclear Strike boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Barracks with a tech lab plus a Ghost Academy, where Cloak is researched and each nuke is bought. 5.0.15 to 5.0.17 changed it back and forth: take the 5.0.17 values.
candidates.shooter_note: An invisible saboteur: one key wipes enemy energy and shields, another lines up a slow heavy shot that a hit interrupts, and a nuke call the target team can see coming.
candidates.repeats: cloak like Jarmen Kell (generals) and the Sentry Drone, fire-power-shot like Anna Kos (iron-harvest), bombard-area like Boris (ra2); the EMP energy burn is new.
candidates.role_guess: anti-infantry (bonus vs Light at 5.0.17); scout or disabler as a secondary

candidates.name: Hellion (with the Hellbat as its second mode)
candidates.teaches: A fast buggy whose flame runs along a line and burns every light unit in it, ideal for worker raids, that stands up into the Hellbat: slower, tougher, a short wide cone of flame, and counted as living, so Medivacs can heal it. Teaches the fast-form and tough-form transform, and a form change that changes which support can fix you. One unit with a Hellbat mode (see coverage_note).

https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Hellbat (infobox: produced at the Factory, Armory needed in versus; Light, Biological, Mechanical)

candidates.role_guess: anti-infantry (bonus vs Light, line splash); raider as a secondary (fast)

candidates.name: Widow Mine
candidates.teaches: A small robot that is itself the mine: it digs in, waits hidden and fires one heavy splash missile at the first enemy in range, then reloads for a long while, shown to the enemy unless upgraded. Teaches the self-placing, re-arming mine and the fear of unseen ground.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Widow_mine (Versus: Activate Mine, Sentinel Missiles, Drilling Claws, Concealment and Deactivate Mine boxes)
https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24078322/starcraft-ii-5-0-13-patch-notes (alert on burrowing, splash radius, reload stealth tied to Drilling Claws)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Factory, no add-on. Staying hidden while reloading needs research (5.0.13 tied it to Drilling Claws; the wiki now lists a Concealment upgrade): check at 5.0.17.
candidates.shooter_note: Plant yourself in a lane and wait unseen; one big shot when an enemy walks over you, then an exposed reload, so placement and patience are the skill.
candidates.repeats: lay-mines like both RA1 Minelayers and the Iron Harvest Engineer, but here the unit is the mine and re-arms itself.

candidates.name: Siege Tank

Teaches minimum range, friendly splash and depending on spotters.

https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (Abduct no longer works on Siege Tanks)

new_mechanics.summary: Press a key on one enemy to lock your guns onto it; they keep firing on their own while you move freely, until a timer ends or the target gets past a leash range, so the fight is about staying close rather than aiming.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Cyclone (Versus: Lock On and Mag-field Accelerator boxes)

candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Factory with a tech lab and an Armory (the registry's own t3 gate). The mode change takes a moment, shortened by Smart Servos research.
candidates.shooter_note: Slow heavy mech: the main gun pounds ground targets, and a mode key decides whether its anti-air throws flak at swarms or slugs at big ships.
candidates.repeats: switch-weapon-mode like the Hammer Tank and Terror Drone (ra3) and the Sentinel (tempest-rising); new here is a choice between two anti-air answers.
candidates.role_guess: anti-air (both modes carry air bonuses); assault as a secondary

candidates.name: Viking
candidates.teaches: A long-range air superiority fighter that can land as a ground walker; each form hits only its own layer, and it can be shot by anti-air while it changes. Teaches the ground-and-air transform built around out-ranging other fliers.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Viking (Versus: Viking Transformation and Smart Servos boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport, built in Fighter (air) mode, which is its base form.
candidates.shooter_note: Fly as a long-range anti-air sniper, then land as a walker to pick at ground targets, timing the change because it leaves you exposed.
candidates.repeats: The same ground-and-air transform as the Mecha Tengu (ra3); its twist is the long-range air duel and the exposed change.

candidates.name: Medivac
candidates.teaches: A dropship that heals living units near it (never machines) and carries a squad or a vehicle, with a short afterburner boost to escape. Teaches carry-and-heal support whose healing depends on what the patient is made of.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Medivac_dropship ("Medivac" redirects here; Versus: Healing, Ignite Afterburners and Caduceus Reactor boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport, no add-on.
candidates.shooter_note: Ferry teammates in, then hover behind them healing the soldiers (not the vehicles); a boost key pulls everyone out when the drop goes wrong.
candidates.repeats: carry-passengers like the Technical and the Thunderhead, repair-allies like the Field Mechanic (ra1), dash like the Tempest Sphere; the twist is healing living units only.

candidates.name: Liberator
candidates.teaches: An air-to-air gunship with splash that can anchor in the sky and project a circle on the ground, where any ground unit that walks in takes heavy single-target shots. Teaches a placed no-go zone cast from the air that ground units answer only by leaving or with anti-air.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Liberator (Versus: Defender Mode, Fighter Mode and Advanced Ballistics boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport, no add-on; Advanced Ballistics is Fusion Core research.
candidates.shooter_note: Fight fliers with splash, or hover in place and lock down a circle of ground; anyone inside gets hammered until they leave or shoot you down.
candidates.repeats: deploy-siege-mode like the Siege Tank and the Siege Chopper (ra2); new is an anchored flier that targets a chosen ground circle.
candidates.role_guess: anti-air; area-denial as a secondary (the Defender Mode circle)

candidates.name: Raven
candidates.teaches: An unarmed flying detector with three tools: a short-lived auto-turret it drops, a matrix that shuts down one machine or psionic unit for a while (research needed since 5.0.12), and a missile that lowers armour in an area. Teaches the unarmed caster: disable, drop a gun, mark for the team.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Raven (Versus: Detector, Interference Matrix, Auto-Turret and Anti-Armor Missile boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport with a tech lab. Its abilities changed in 4.0 and 4.1.4 (see coverage_note): code the current set.
candidates.shooter_note: No gun: you win by shutting down the enemy's best machine, dropping a turret into the fight and cracking armour for your team, while uncovering cloaked foes.
candidates.repeats: deploy-turret like William Mason and the Shieldmaiden, disable-machine like the Terror Drone (ra3); the twist is an unarmed detector caster.

candidates.name: Banshee
candidates.teaches: A strike gunship that hits only ground targets and, after research, cloaks at the cost of energy, so it harasses until detection arrives or its energy runs dry. Teaches a time-limited cloak that forces the enemy to invest in detection.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/AH/G-24_Banshee ("Banshee" redirects here; Versus: Cloaking Field and Hyperflight Rotors boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport with a tech lab, where Cloaking Field and Hyperflight Rotors are researched.
candidates.shooter_note: Cloak in, rocket workers or artillery, and leave before the energy bar empties or a detector shows you.
candidates.repeats: cloak like Jarmen Kell, the Sentry Drone and Olga Morozova; the twist is an energy-draining cloak on an air gunship.
candidates.role_guess: assault by the steps (stock speed is medium); raider in practice

candidates.name: Battlecruiser
candidates.teaches: A slow capital ship that fires while moving, can jump anywhere on the map after a short spell in which it can still be hit, and after research fires one heavy Yamato blast. Teaches map-wide repositioning with a vulnerable wind-up, and a capital-ship power shot.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Battlecruiser_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Yamato Cannon, Tactical Jump and Weapon Refit boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Starport with a tech lab and a Fusion Core (Weapon Refit, researched there, unlocks the Yamato).
candidates.shooter_note: A flying fortress you steer slowly while it shoots on the move; one key warps you across the map to defend or flee, another fires a huge shot at one target.
candidates.repeats: fire-power-shot like Anna Kos, teleport like the Chrono Legionnaire and the Vimana; new is a map-wide jump with a visible delay.

candidates.name: Zergling
candidates.teaches: The cheapest swarm melee creature, sold two per purchase, very fast once upgraded and built to surround; it can morph one way into a Baneling. Teaches a swarm body count and the one-way morph into another unit.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Zergling_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Metabolic Boost, Adrenal Glands and Baneling Morph boxes)
https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (no Zergling change; the patch of record)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva once a Spawning Pool stands, two per purchase (body count 2).
candidates.shooter_note: A cheap, fast biter that wins by surrounding; one key turns you for good into a Baneling when the fight calls for a bomb.
candidates.repeats: upgrade-in-field like the Red Guard and the Overlord (generals); patterns.md folds morphs into upgrade-in-field, and no unit in the data morphs into another.
candidates.role_guess: assault by the steps (raider once Metabolic Boost is researched)

candidates.name: Baneling
candidates.teaches: A rolling acid bomb that dies to blow up crowds of light units without harming friends; it can lie burrowed as a living mine and detonate from underground, and a toggle lets it go for buildings. Teaches cheap mass suicide splash and the buried ambush.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Baneling (Versus: Explode, Enable Attack Building and Centrifugal Hooks boxes; notes that its splash spares friends)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); morphed from a Zergling with a Baneling Nest (a unit of its own by the plan); its price counts the Zergling's share (registry morph rule).
candidates.shooter_note: A sprinting bomb: roll into a crowd and pop, or bury yourself in a lane and go off when they walk over; one life, huge payoff.
candidates.repeats: self-destruct like the MAD Tank (ra1); the twist is a cheap mass bomb that can wait buried as a mine and never hurts friends.

candidates.name: Roach
candidates.teaches: A cheap, tough ranged brute that heals very fast while burrowed and, after research, crawls underground unseen. Teaches burrow-to-heal and tunnelling past defences, answered only by detection.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Roach (Versus: Tunneling Claws, Roach Regeneration, Glial Reconstitution and Ravager Morph boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with a Roach Warren. Burrow itself is game-wide research; moving while burrowed is the Roach's own upgrade.
candidates.shooter_note: Brawl, then duck underground to heal and sneak forward under the fight; enemies need a detector to stop you.
candidates.repeats: heal-self like the Stark (iron-harvest) and burrow like the RA1 Submarine; the burrow-and-heal pairing is new.

candidates.name: Ravager
candidates.teaches: A morph of the Roach that lobs Corrosive Bile: a blob that lands on a chosen spot after a visible delay, hitting ground and air there and breaking Force Fields. Teaches a dodgeable skill-shot bombard on a frontline unit.
pages: https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (one bile now breaks a Force Field)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); morphed from a Roach (Roach Warren); its price counts the Roach's.
candidates.shooter_note: Every few seconds, mark a spot for an acid shell that lands a moment later: punish anyone standing still, scatter clumps, smash barriers.
candidates.repeats: bombard-area like Boris (ra2) and the Nakovalnya; new is a short-cooldown, dodgeable bombard on a cheap line unit that also breaks walls.
candidates.role_guess: assault; siege as a secondary (Corrosive Bile)

candidates.name: Hydralisk
candidates.teaches: A fragile, hard-hitting ranged creature that shoots ground and air, with a short Lunge burst after research (since 5.0.14) and the one-way morph into the Lurker. Teaches the glass cannon that needs protecting.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Hydralisk_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Lunge, Muscular Augments, Grooved Spines and Lurker Morph boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with a Hydralisk Den (Lair).
candidates.shooter_note: High damage against anything, ground or air, but it melts: stay behind tougher teammates and use the lunge to reposition.
candidates.repeats: A both-layer ranged generalist like the Marine; dash like the Tempest Sphere; the twist is glass-cannon damage and the Lurker morph.

candidates.name: Lurker
candidates.teaches: A morph of the Hydralisk that can attack only while burrowed, driving spines along a line that hit everything in it, unseen unless detected. Teaches the hidden zone holder: dig in, and the ground in front of you is lethal.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Lurker_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Burrowed Attack, Adaptive Talons and Seismic Spines boxes; infobox Subterranean Spines)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); morphed from a Hydralisk with a Lurker Den; it burrows without the Burrow research.
candidates.shooter_note: Burrow at a choke and spear lines of enemies from cover they cannot see; once a detector arrives you are a sitting target.
candidates.repeats: deploy-siege-mode and burrow both exist in the data, but not a hidden deploy with a piercing line attack.
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (bonus vs Armored); area-denial as a secondary

candidates.name: Queen
candidates.teaches: A slow home-defence caster that heals living units and buildings, plants creep tumours that spread the Zerg's fast ground, and makes a Hatchery spawn extra larvae; quick on creep, crawling off it. Teaches team-economy support and terrain your own side spreads.

new_mechanics.summary: Plant or drip a growth that spreads ground over time on which your side moves faster and can see, and which enemies must find and clear; patterns.md lists StarCraft II creep as not added for now.
Target a friendly production building so it turns out extra units, or faster spawns, for a while; in a shooter, speeding up teammates' respawns at a base.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Queen_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Create Creep Tumor, Spawn Larva and Transfusion boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); made at a Hatchery, Lair or Hive (not from Larva) with a Spawning Pool.
candidates.shooter_note: A base guardian: patch up teammates, spread fast ground for the team and speed up your base's output; step off the creep and you crawl.
candidates.repeats: repair-allies like the Field Mechanic and the Shieldmaiden; creep spreading and larva injection have no example in the data.
candidates.role_guess: support (Transfusion); anti-air as a secondary (hits air)

candidates.name: Overlord
candidates.teaches: An unarmed, very slow flying beast whose existence raises the Zerg army cap; it scouts, can drip creep below itself, and each one can be upgraded to carry units. Killing Overlords blocks Zerg production. Teaches a unit whose value is the team's cap rather than its combat.

new_mechanics.summary: Simply staying alive raises your team's unit or population cap; when it dies the team cannot add units until it is replaced, so enemies hunt it to stall the whole side.

As for the Queen; here the Overlord drips creep on the ground beneath it. Plant or drip a growth that spreads ground over time on which your side moves faster and can see, and which enemies must find and clear; patterns.md lists StarCraft II creep as not added for now.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overlord_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Pneumatized Carapace, Mutate Ventral Sacs, Overseer Morph and Excrete Creep boxes; infobox supply)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with no requirement; passenger seats only after Mutate Ventral Sacs (Lair) is bought on that Overlord.
candidates.shooter_note: A floating supply node: stay alive and scout for the team; with the upgrade you become a slow troop carrier.
candidates.repeats: carry-passengers like the Thunderhead and the Sudden Transport; the cap mechanic has no example in the data.
candidates.role_guess: no clean role (an unarmed supply provider): scout, or transport after the upgrade; a fit note is likely

candidates.name: Overseer
candidates.teaches: A flying detector morphed from an Overlord that spawns Changelings (fake enemy soldiers that walk among the enemy as spies), slimes an enemy building so it stops producing for a while, and can stop to see much farther. Teaches spy decoys and stalling buildings.

new_mechanics.summary: Slime or jam an enemy building from range so it cannot produce, research or work for a while, without damaging it; a fit for a base-assault economy.

As for the Overlord; the Overseer keeps providing supply. Simply staying alive raises your team's unit or population cap; when it dies the team cannot add units until it is replaced, so enemies hunt it to stall the whole side.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Overseer (Versus: Detector, Contaminate, Spawn Changeling and Oversight Mode boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); morphed from an Overlord (Lair). The Changeling is coded with it (closed list).
candidates.shooter_note: The team's eye in the sky: uncover cloaked enemies, send fake enemy soldiers to spy, and slime an enemy factory shut before a push.
candidates.repeats: disguise like the RA1 Spy and the Sudden Transport, but through a separate spawned decoy; Oversight Mode links deploy-siege-mode as a sight variant (the merge pass may prefer a variant name).

candidates.name: Mutalisk
candidates.teaches: A fast flying harasser whose glaive hits a target and bounces on to two more, and which regenerates much faster than other Zerg. Teaches the bouncing attack and hit-and-run by regeneration.
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with a Spire (Lair).
candidates.shooter_note: Dart in, bounce glaives through a cluster, fly off to heal and come back; splash and dedicated anti-air punish a clumped flock.
candidates.repeats: No unit in the data has a bouncing attack (weapon trait chain); its quick regeneration is the self-repair armour model every Zerg has, stronger here.

candidates.name: Corruptor
candidates.teaches: An air-only flier strongest against big Massive ships that can also channel a ramping acid spray on buildings, and morphs one way into the Brood Lord. Teaches a dedicated anti-capital-ship counter with a structure-only side job.

new_mechanics.summary: Hold a spray or beam on one target; its damage climbs the longer it stays on, and breaking off resets it (an ability form of the charge-up weapon trait).

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Corruptor (Versus: Caustic Spray and Brood Lord Morph boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with a Spire.
candidates.shooter_note: Hunt the enemy's biggest fliers; when the sky is clear, hover over a building and melt it with a channel that keeps growing.
candidates.repeats: upgrade-in-field like the Zergling's morph; the anti-Massive focus and the ramping channel are new.

candidates.name: Brood Lord
candidates.teaches: A slow flying siege beast morphed from a Corruptor whose shots hatch short-lived Broodlings on the ground that attack ground units and get in their way. Teaches attacks that spawn blockers, and an air siege unit helpless against anti-air.
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); morphed from a Corruptor with a Greater Spire; its price counts the Corruptor's. The Broodling is coded with it (closed list).
candidates.shooter_note: Hang back in the air and rain broodlings that tie up and chew ground enemies; any anti-air that reaches you ends you.
candidates.repeats: Its weapon is the drone-launcher family (the registry correction keeps launch-drones for key-driven drones), as the Carrier's is; spawning ground blockers is new.

candidates.name: Infestor
candidates.teaches: An unarmed caster (no weapon at 5.0.17) that moves while burrowed, nets a group with Fungal Growth (a heavy slow with damage that also uncovers hidden units and blocks blinks, jumps, burrowing and boarding), takes over one enemy unit while it keeps channelling, and covers friendly ground units with a cloud that halves ranged damage. Teaches crowd control, borrowing an enemy unit through a tether, and shielding allies.

new_mechanics.summary: On a key, hit an area so every enemy in it is badly slowed and hurt over a few seconds and cannot blink, jump, burrow or board a transport, and hidden ones show up: a net that pins a group for teammates. patterns.md folds stun, root and slow into weapon traits, but no pattern holds the ability version; block-abilities overlaps only on the blocked escapes.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Infestor (Versus: Fungal Growth, Neural Parasite, Microbial Shroud and Burrowed Movement boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with an Infestation Pit. Its infobox still lists infested terrans, removed in 4.11.0, and the 5.0.16 weapon is gone at 5.0.17.
candidates.shooter_note: Tunnel under the fight, pop up to net a group for your team, borrow an enemy's best unit while you hold the channel, or cover allies with a damage-cutting cloud.
candidates.repeats: mind-control like Yuri's Mastermind (ra2), but channelled through one tether; Microbial Shroud links rally-allies as the Sentry's Guardian Shield does in data/patterns/rally-allies.json (raise-shield is the alternative).

candidates.name: Swarm Host
candidates.teaches: A host with no weapon that, on a long cooldown, releases a pair of free, short-lived Locusts that fly over terrain and must land to attack, so it wears an enemy down from far away. Teaches attrition by free timed minions while the summoner stays out of reach.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Swarm_host (Versus text: Locusts released on the move by hand; Flying Locusts box)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with an Infestation Pit. Campaign strains (Deep Tunnel and others) are not versus. The Locust is coded with it (closed list).
candidates.shooter_note: Stay hidden, send waves of short-lived flying biters on a cooldown, and relocate; if the enemy ignores the waves and dives you, you have no defence.
candidates.repeats: launch-drones like the Drone Operator and the Vimana (tempest-rising); its twist is free timed waves on a long cooldown from a weaponless host.

candidates.name: Viper
candidates.teaches: An unarmed flying caster that yanks one unit to itself (Abduct), drops a cloud that cuts enemy ground ranged units down to melee reach, sets a parasite on a flier that hurts the fliers around it, and refuels by draining its own buildings. Teaches pulls and range denial.

new_mechanics.summary: Draw health from a friendly building to refill your own ability energy; the building can be healed later, so energy is bought with team resources.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Viper (Versus: Abduct, Blinding Cloud, Consume and Parasitic Bomb boxes)
https://news.blizzard.com/en-us/article/24309308/starcraft-ii-5-0-17-patch-notes (Abduct no longer works on Siege Tanks)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with a Hive.
candidates.shooter_note: Hook an enemy tank or hero into your team, blind a firing line with a cloud, punish clumped fliers; top up energy back at base.
candidates.repeats: pull-target like the Magnetron (ra2) and lay-smoke like the Mocny (iron-harvest); infest-vehicle is the registry's own listing for Parasitic Bomb (leave-hazard-zone fits too, for the merge pass).

candidates.name: Ultralisk
candidates.teaches: A huge melee beast whose blades cleave through crowds and which shrugs off slows, stuns and mind control; it cannot touch fliers. Teaches crowd-control immunity as a defining trait.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Ultralisk_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Frenzied, Chitinous Plating and Anabolic Synthesis boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); from Larva with an Ultralisk Cavern (Hive).
candidates.shooter_note: A walking battering ram: wade into groups, cleave them apart and ignore the snares and stuns that stop everyone else; fliers kite you freely.
candidates.repeats: A brute like the Stark (iron-harvest) and the Tempest Sphere; the immunity is coded with immune: links, not a pattern.

candidates.name: Zealot
candidates.teaches: A shielded melee warrior that, after research, charges at an enemy to close the gap fast; it can be warped in at any power field. Teaches the gap-closing charge and recharging shields on a melee frontliner.
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Gateway, or warped in after the Warp Gate research; Charge is researched at the Twilight Council.
candidates.shooter_note: Melee frontliner whose charge snaps onto a nearby target; back off for a moment and your shields refill.
candidates.repeats: dash with delivery ram, as patterns.md folds charges (the Tempest Sphere links dash); a plain melee charger is new to the data.

candidates.name: Stalker
candidates.teaches: A fast ranged walker that hits ground and air, with bonus damage against armoured units, and after research Blink: a short instant teleport to chase, escape, cross cliffs or pull a hurt Stalker to the back. Teaches the short tactical blink.
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Gateway with a Cybernetics Core; Blink is researched at the Twilight Council.
candidates.shooter_note: Poke from range, blink in to finish or out to save your shields, and blink up cliffs to escape ground chasers.
candidates.repeats: teleport like the Chrono Legionnaire (ra2), the Thunderhead and the Vimana; its twist is a very short, instant combat blink.
candidates.role_guess: anti-armour (bonus vs Armored); anti-air as a secondary

candidates.name: Sentry
candidates.teaches: A floating support robot with three team tools: energy walls that block movement (split an army, seal a ramp), an aura that cuts incoming ranged damage, and hallucinated copies of units for scouting and feints. Teaches battlefield-shaping walls and decoys.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Sentry (Force Field, Guardian Shield and Hallucination boxes; the page has no Versus heading, the boxes sit under Wings of Liberty)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Gateway with a Cybernetics Core. The campaign's shield-recharge abilities are not versus.
candidates.shooter_note: Throw walls to cut enemies off or plug a choke, shield your front line against bullets, or send fake units ahead to scout and bait.
candidates.repeats: build-cover like the Iron Harvest Engineer (energy-wall variant), rally-allies like the Line Officer; spawn-decoy has no unit in the data yet.

candidates.name: Adept
candidates.teaches: A light-slaying infantry unit that projects an invulnerable shade it can steer and, after a delay, teleports to it unless it calls it off. Teaches the feint teleport: commit, or cancel and keep the enemy guessing.
pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/Adept (Versus: Psionic Transfer and Resonating Glaives boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Gateway with a Cybernetics Core.
candidates.shooter_note: Send your shade into the enemy backline, watch them react, then teleport in or cancel; deadly against light units and workers.
candidates.repeats: teleport like the Stalker; patterns.md already folds the steerable, cancellable shade into teleport.
candidates.role_guess: anti-infantry (bonus vs Light); raider as a secondary

candidates.name: High Templar
candidates.teaches: A frail psionic caster whose Psionic Storm hurts every unit in an area over a few seconds, friends included; Feedback empties a target's energy and damages it for what it emptied; two Templar can merge into an Archon. Teaches area denial with friendly fire, energy burn and merging.

new_mechanics.summary: As for the Ghost; Feedback empties one target's energy and turns half of it into damage. Hit an area or one enemy so its ability energy is emptied (in some versions its energy shields too), leaving casters unable to cast until it builds back; some versions turn the emptied energy into damage.

Two units fuse into one stronger unit that keeps their combined price; for players, two teammates could pool into one shared body. research/registry-notes/patterns.md lists the Archon merge as not added for now.

pages: https://starcraft.fandom.com/wiki/High_templar_(StarCraft_II) (Versus: Psionic Storm, Feedback and Archon Warp boxes)
candidates.skirmish: Buildable in skirmish against the AI and in every multiplayer mode (ladder, custom games, Archon mode); Gateway with Templar Archives, where Psionic Storm is researched.
candidates.shooter_note: A glass-cannon spellcaster: drop storms to deny ground (and keep your team out of them), burn enemy casters' energy, or merge with a teammate into an Archon.
candidates.repeats: leave-hazard-zone like the Desolator (ra2); the energy burn and the merge are new.

candidates.name: Dark Templar
candidates.teaches: A melee assassin that is always invisible, so detection is the only answer; after research it blinks a short way; two can merge into an Archon. Teaches permanent stealth (the stealth sensor trait, not a cloak key) and a hard detection check.

new_mechanics.summary: As for the High Templar (Archon Warp). Two units fuse into one stronger unit that keeps their combined price; for players, two teammates could pool into one shared body. research/registry-notes/patterns.md lists the Archon merge as not added for now.

HELLION AND HELLBAT: ONE UNIT, sc2.terran.hellion, with a Hellbat mode (modes[].via transform). The rule that decides is the modes[] rule in docs/fields.md: "Second forms that change how the unit moves or what it is: deploy, siege and transform modes. The base form is the form the unit is built or bought in; if it can be built in either, it is the form whose name the unit carries." Why: (1) In versus every Hellion can switch to Hellbat and back with one shared button (Hellion Transformation, Armory needed; Versus ability box on the StarCraft Wiki's Hellion and Hellbat pages), and the switch changes how it moves (wheels and fast, to legs and medium speed) and what it is (it gains the Biological attribute, so Medivacs heal it, and its flame turns from a line into a cone): a transform mode in the rule's own words. (2) The rule's second sentence foresees a unit that can be built in either form, which the Hellbat can be (its infobox: made at the Factory, Armory needed in versus), and answers with a base form, not a second entry; calibration round 1 wrote that sentence for this very case (research/pilot/round-1/analysis/structure.json, finding modes-parts, names the Hellion or Hellbat). (3) The name the unit carries is Hellion: the shared button is Hellion Transformation, the Hellbat page calls it a transforming vehicle based on the hellion and formerly the battle hellion, and the registry already calls the Hellbat the Hellion's second mode (data/games.json sc2 source note; games-r4.md). By the Ids rule the slug is that in-game name, so the id is sc2.terran.hellion; the one Ids clause that splits a type into several entries (stock parts that differ by side) does not apply. The abilities rule (two buttons that undo each other are one entry) and Paired entries (the Hellbat flame is an alternate weapon with the mode, both linking transform) then code it, as data/patterns/transform.json already lists "Hellion / Hellbat". The plan's morph sentence does not reach it: its examples are one-way morphs into another unit, while this switch is reversible at will, like the Viking's.

DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE CURRENT MULTIPLAYER ROSTER AND THIS LIST. (a) Left out by the plan: the workers (SCV, Drone, Probe); the MULE; the Larva and the Cocoon (covering every Zerg egg and cocoon: Baneling, Ravager, Lurker, Overseer, Brood Lord); the Changeling, Locust, Broodling and Interceptor, coded with the Overseer, Swarm Host, Brood Lord and Carrier (Broodlings that burst from dead Zerg buildings are a building effect). (b) Merged by the field rules: the Hellbat, a mode of the Hellion, so the game's 16 Terran unit buttons give 15 entries. (c) Not units: the Raven's Auto-Turret, the Oracle's Stasis Ward, the Queen's Creep Tumor, the Adept's shade, the Sentry's hallucinations and the Disruptor's nova are coded with their maker; the Nydus Worm, the Spine and Spore Crawlers (buildings that can uproot and crawl) and the Terran buildings that lift off are structures and stay out. (d) Removed by patches, so not coded: the Mothership Core left multiplayer in patch 4.0 (StarCraft Wiki: the Mothership core page and the Patch 4.0.0 history page), and since then the Mothership is built straight at the Nexus with a Fleet Beacon; the Infestor's Infested Terran spawn went in 4.11.0, replaced by Microbial Shroud (the wiki's Patch 4.11.0 history page); the Raven's Seeker Missile and Point Defense Drone went in 4.0 and its Repair Drone, added in 4.0, went in 4.1.4 (the wiki's Patch 4.0.0 history page; the cached Liquipedia Raven (Legacy of the Void) page, Patch Changes), but the wiki's Point defense drone page dates the drone's removal to 4.1.4, so the sources disagree on that date. (e) Added by patches: none since Legacy of the Void's release on 10 November 2015, which brought the Adept, Cyclone, Disruptor, Liberator, Lurker and Ravager into versus (the StarCraft Wiki's page on the expansion, its box of versus units). Patches 5.0.15 to 5.0.17 add or remove no unit (Blizzard's 5.0.17 notes and 5.0.15 hotfix notes, read; the wiki's 5.0.x version history). What does change at 5.0.17: 5.0.16 gave the Infestor a weapon and the Disruptor a phantom weapon and 5.0.17 took both away, so both are unarmed; 5.0.12 reworked the Cyclone and 5.0.14 restored its 5.0.11 form; 5.0.12 took the Mothership's energy (cooldown spells, an active Cloaking Field); 5.0.16b reverted Load Nearby Units on the Overlord, Medivac and Warp Prism.
